criteria.criterion: per-concentration fitted ex, C, R2 for at least 3 concentrations, listed one by one; primary arm = rate-dependent crushing n = 0.33
criteria.note: C is the prefactor at A_0 = 1 m2 (MPa); R2 is the coefficient of determination of the log-log regression; the per-concentration numbers are in rows and in pressure_area_fit.csv

criteria.criterion: relative deviation of the fitted ex/C from the ISO 19906 value, per concentration; > 15 % is a FAIL with an attribution
criteria.reason: the normative numbers are not available (no primary text, no transcription with clause/table locators -- see anchor.required_documents), so the deviation from the standard cannot be computed. The table reports the deviation from the DECLARED reference normalisation (C_R = 1 MPa, ex = -0.28; not normative) and from the ecosystem's UNVERIFIED candidate (ex = -0.30, quote = null, comparison only); neither may be presented as the standard's value.
criteria.note: reading the 15 % threshold mechanically is only valid against the declared reference / candidate; if a row exceeds it, the conclusion is 'differs from the declared reference', never 'differs from ISO'

criteria.criterion: ensemble of at least 15 impacts per concentration; parameter distribution reported as median with 5-95 % quantiles
criteria.note: impact counts are pooled over all seeds of a concentration; quantiles are taken over the per-seed fits (each seed fitting its own impacts) with quantile_summary (linear interpolation)

criteria.criterion: global vs local pressure calibre bridged item by item; incomparable items marked WITHHELD with a reason

rows.value: the model carries no sub-patch pressure field, so neither the high-pressure-zone area A_loc nor its internal pressure distribution exists; p_loc cannot be sampled

kappa_demo.note: kappa = 1 in the simulated model (single uniform pressure over the contact patch), so a local-calibre (high-pressure-zone) comparison is WITHHELD

bridge.summary: the simulated side has the global calibre only; the local calibre and the standard's validity range are WITHHELD. Any ex comparison must first align (i) the area definition, (ii) the pressure calibre, (iii) the population / A range and (iv) the C normalisation point -- missing any one makes the comparison meaningless.

limitations: the contact patch carries a SINGLE uniform pressure: the model's p can only be the global (area-average) calibre, there is no high-pressure-zone / non-simultaneous contact structure, so a local-calibre ex cannot be sampled from this chain

the pressure source is a declared engineering constitutive law: p_ref, epsdot_ref and n are declared inputs and the pressure level scales exactly linearly in p_ref; n is swept (0.15 / 0.33 / 0.50) as a sensitivity, not calibrated to ice measurements
floes are point masses, the ice is level and homogeneous and no floe-size statistics of the crushed layer are resolved

ex is a POPULATION-dependent quantity: the raw p-A slope mixes in the co-variation of thickness and closing speed, and the multifactor decomposition separates the mechanism-level partial exponent dlnp/dlnA; any reported ex must state its population

the primary ISO 19906 text is not reachable -> the quantitative deviation from the standard is WITHHELD; every 'standard value' slot is left empty and in-ecosystem candidates are used for comparison only (quote = null)
the hydrodynamic / radiation model is still the declared synthetic W23 model: this node is about the ice contact statistics, so the hull response quantities are not a full-scale validation

figures.caption: impact pressure vs nominal contact area (log-log) for the closure arm C1, the negative control C0 and the primary rate-dependent arm T (n = 0.33), with the fitted power laws and the declared normalisation line; the imposed-law arm collapses exactly onto its own line (R2 = 1), the rate-dependent arm does not

fitted exponent per ice concentration and arm: median with 5-95 % quantiles over the per-seed fits; dotted grey lines are the analytic -n of the rate law and the dashed line the declared (non-normative) normalisation ex = -0.28

multifactor log-log decomposition of the rate-dependent arms: the partial area exponent dlnp/dlnA recovers -n while the raw p(A) slope is confounded by the thickness and the closing speed (confounding is the main finding)
